read_chat_activity.title: Chat activity
read_chat_activity.description: How much traffic each room has seen, newest post first, with the totals over the whole filtered set rather than over the page.

list_chat_threads.title: A room's threads
list_chat_threads.description: Every thread in one structure's room the caller may read, oldest first, each with its label, its audience and its unread count for the caller: the posts somebody else wrote after the caller's read point. A thread still with the leads is listed only to the structure's leads and to the actor who asked for it. Only for a caller the mount says belongs to that structure. A structure the caller does not belong to and one that does not exist answer identically, as a not-found.

args.description: The structure whose room this is.

start_chat_thread.title: Start a thread
start_chat_thread.description: Starts a thread with a label in one structure's room, for a caller the mount says leads that structure. The thread begins readable by the structure's leads only, until one of them opens it to the group. A label the room already has, in any case or spacing, answers with that thread rather than a second one. A caller who does not lead the structure, one who does not belong to it and a structure that does not exist answer identically, as a not-found.

args.description: The structure whose room this is.
The thread's name, as the room's thread list shows it.

open_chat_thread.title: Open a thread to the group
open_chat_thread.description: Opens a thread that only the structure's leads could read to everybody who belongs to the structure, keeping every post written before. Opening a thread that is already the group's answers with it unchanged. Only a caller the mount says leads the structure may open one; anybody else, a thread that was never minted and a thread of another structure all answer the same not-found.

args.description: The structure whose room this is.
The thread, which must belong to that structure's room.

request_chat_thread.title: Ask for a thread
request_chat_thread.description: Asks for a thread on a topic in one structure's room, for any caller the mount says belongs to that structure. The thread begins readable by the structure's leads and by the caller who asked, beside each other, until a lead opens it to the group or declines it. Every lead the mount names for the structure is told through a notification naming the thread. A topic the room already has in a thread the caller may read answers with that thread and tells nobody; a topic held by a thread the caller may not read is given a thread of its own, so asking never reveals one. A structure the caller does not belong to and one that does not exist answer identically, as a not-found.

args.description: The structure whose room this is.
The caller, from the session, who becomes the thread's requester.
What the thread is for, as the room's thread list shows it.

decline_chat_thread.title: Decline a thread request
decline_chat_thread.description: Closes a thread somebody asked for, still with the leads, without opening it. From then on it is listed to nobody and every address answers it as one that was never minted, and the caller who asked for it is told through a notification naming the thread and the lead who declined. Declining a thread already declined answers with it unchanged and tells nobody again. A thread that is already the group's, or that nobody asked for, is refused as a conflict. Only a caller the mount says leads the structure may decline one; anybody else, a thread that was never minted and a thread of another structure all answer the same not-found.

args.description: The structure whose room this is.
The thread, which must belong to that structure's room.

list_chat_messages.title: Posts in a thread
list_chat_messages.description: Every post in one thread of a structure's room, oldest first, for a caller who belongs to that structure. An outsider, a thread that was never minted and a thread of another structure all answer the same not-found.

args.description: The structure whose room this is.
The thread, which must belong to that structure's room.

post_chat_message.title: Post in a thread
post_chat_message.description: Posts one message to a thread of a structure's room the caller belongs to. The author is the session's: a body naming another author is ignored, so nobody can post as somebody else.

args.description: The structure whose room this is.
The thread, which must belong to that structure's room.

mark_chat_thread_read.title: Mark a thread read
mark_chat_thread_read.description: Moves the caller's own read point in one thread of a structure's room they belong to, up to the post the body names or, naming none, up to now. The point never moves backwards. The reader is the session's: nobody marks a thread read for somebody else. An outsider, a thread that was never minted and a post of another thread all answer the same not-found.

args.description: The structure whose room this is.
The thread, which must belong to that structure's room.
The last post the reader has seen, which must be in this thread. Absent marks everything posted until now as read.

open_subject_thread.title: Open a thread about a subject
open_subject_thread.description: Returns the caller's private thread on a subject, or the subject's group thread, opening it the first time. A private thread is always the caller's own. A caller the host gives no standing on the subject, and a subject that does not exist, answer the same not-found.

args.description: What kind of thing the subject is, in the host's own vocabulary.
Which thing of that kind the conversation is about.
private, for a thread between the caller and whoever answers for the subject; group, for the thread everyone the subject reached can read.

list_subject_threads.title: Threads about a subject
list_subject_threads.description: The threads about one subject the caller may read, each with its message count and the time of its last message. Somebody the subject reached sees the group thread and their own private one; whoever answers for the subject sees every thread.

args.description: What kind of thing the subject is, in the host's own vocabulary.
Which thing of that kind the conversation is about.

list_subject_messages.title: Messages on a subject thread
list_subject_messages.description: Every message on one thread about a subject, oldest first. A message posted by whoever answers for the subject carries no author for anybody else, so it reads as the answering side's. A thread the caller may not read and one that was never opened answer the same not-found.

post_subject_message.title: Post on a subject thread
post_subject_message.description: Posts one message to a thread about a subject the caller may read, and tells everyone it replies to through their notifications: on a private thread, the one it is with when the answering side posts, and everyone the host names as answering for the subject when the one it is with posts; on a group thread, everyone else from the subject's audience who has posted there. The author is the session's.

args.description: An optional finer reference inside the subject the message is about. Empty means the subject as a whole.

list_dm_threads.title: My conversations
list_dm_threads.description: Every conversation the caller is currently invited to or active in. Each row carries only the caller's own address index, never the other party's.

get_dm_thread.title: One conversation
get_dm_thread.description: One conversation the caller is on the roster of. A conversation that exists but the caller is not on, and one that was never minted, answer identically — the status code must not become an enumeration oracle.

list_dm_participants.title: Who is on a conversation
list_dm_participants.description: Every participant's standing on one conversation, for a caller who is on its roster.

invite_to_dm_thread.title: Invite somebody
invite_to_dm_thread.description: Admin-only. Invites one actor onto a conversation, or returns an already-active one to invited without disturbing their admin flag.

args.description: The admin issuing the invite, from the session.

accept_dm_invite.title: Accept an invite
accept_dm_invite.description: The caller accepts their own invite. Nobody can accept on somebody else's behalf, because the actor is the session's and not the body's.

leave_dm_thread.title: Leave a conversation
leave_dm_thread.description: The caller leaves. Refused when the caller is the only active admin and other participants are still active, since every roster write needs an admin and nobody could restore one.

kick_from_dm_thread.title: Remove somebody
kick_from_dm_thread.description: Admin-only, and a self-kick is refused — leaving is the act for that, and it carries the last-admin rule a kick would bypass.

args.description: The admin issuing it, from the session.

promote_dm_participant.title: Make somebody an admin
promote_dm_participant.description: Admin-only. A plain update rather than an upsert: promoting somebody who was never on the roster is a not-found, never a silently created row.

args.description: The admin issuing it, from the session.

reenable_dm_participant.title: Rejoin or readmit
reenable_dm_participant.description: An admin returns somebody to invited. A departed participant re-enabling themselves is allowed only while nobody else is active, and that claim is one conditional statement so two of them cannot both win.

args.description: Who to re-enable. Absent means the caller themselves, which is how a departed participant rejoins.

list_dm_messages.title: Messages on a conversation
list_dm_messages.description: Every message still within its deadline, oldest first, for a caller who is active on the roster. The timer is read off the conversation, where it was frozen when the conversation opened.

publish_dm_device_key.title: Publish a device key
publish_dm_device_key.description: Publishes one of the caller's handset keys. The owner, the publisher and the handset are session facts: a body claiming any of them is overwritten rather than refused.

lookup_dm_device_keys.title: Look up device keys
lookup_dm_device_keys.description: Every live key for the actors named, so a sender can seal a message to each of their handsets. Retired keys are never returned.

list_dm_reactions.title: Reactions on a conversation
list_dm_reactions.description: Every reaction on every message of one conversation, for a caller who is active on the roster.

set_dm_reaction.title: React to a message
set_dm_reaction.description: Sets the caller's own reaction to one message, replacing whatever they had on it. The reactor is the session's, so nobody can react as somebody else.

clear_dm_reaction.title: Take a reaction back
clear_dm_reaction.description: Clears the caller's own reaction to one message, and only their own.

list_report_queue.title: The moderation queue
list_report_queue.description: Every post somebody has asked the moderators of one structure to look at, newest first.

list_reports_for_message.title: Reports against one post
list_reports_for_message.description: Every report filed against one post, newest first.

args.description: The structure whose queue the post sits in.

list_my_addresses.title: My addresses
list_my_addresses.description: The caller's own view of every address they hold, retired ones included. The plaintext comes back only for an address its owner asked to be held.

retire_my_address.title: Retire an address
retire_my_address.description: Stops one of the caller's own addresses accepting new conversations. Conversations already open under it keep working — retiring must never sever one the other party is in the middle of.

args.description: Which of the caller's own addresses.

list_notifications.title: My notifications
list_notifications.description: The caller's own notifications, newest first. There is no stored title or body: a client renders both from the event and the subject it names.

count_unread_notifications.title: My unread badge
count_unread_notifications.description: How many of the caller's own notifications are unread.

mark_notifications_read.title: Mark notifications read
mark_notifications_read.description: Marks some of the caller's own notifications read, and reports how many it moved. Read is the recipient's own assertion and the only column a client writes.

args.description: When they were read, RFC3339. Absent means now, from the server's clock.

list_notification_preferences.title: My notification settings
list_notification_preferences.description: Which categories the caller has muted. A category with no row is on, because absent is on.

set_notification_preference.title: Mute or unmute a category
set_notification_preference.description: Mutes or unmutes one category for the caller. A category the mounted domain does not declare is a not-found; one the domain marks exempt is refused with the reason rather than stored as unmuted.

subscribe_push.title: Subscribe this browser to pushes
subscribe_push.description: Stores one of the caller's browser push subscriptions, so that every notification raised for the caller is also sent to this browser as a Web Push. The body is the browser's PushSubscription as it serialises it; the subscriber and the handset are session facts, so a body naming anybody else is ignored. Re-subscribing an endpoint replaces it, and an endpoint somebody else held becomes the caller's.

args.description: The push service URL the browser minted.
The browser's p256dh public key and auth secret, base64url.

unsubscribe_push.title: Stop pushes to this browser
unsubscribe_push.description: Removes one of the caller's own push subscriptions by its endpoint. An endpoint the caller does not hold is left alone and answers the same, so the call is safe to repeat.

args.description: The push service URL to stop sending to.
